judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures check out exactly against the artifacts. Problem 2 prints 'Tell a friend why 12 cannot be a part of 9. Then write the part that really goes in the circle.' and verify.json id 2 is a single eval of 9-3 -> 6; final_response.md then asserts 'Nothing is flagged manual --- every item on this sheet has a single checkable number', which is not true of the first sentence of problem 2. Problems 3 and 4 each print 'Cross out the fact Ben wrote twice' / 'Cross out the repeat' as a required marked response, and verify.json ids 3 and 4 each hold one eval entry covering only the replacement number (7 and 4). The judge's mathematics is also right: I recomputed 2, 6, 7, 4, 3 and the pair 3 and 5, plus the three study-guide try-its (2, 6, whole 7), and every value agrees with the printed key. The trap values are genuinely distinguishable from the correct answers. REJECT on the trust boundary is correct even though the mathematics is clean.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 6 is the counter-example that proves the fix is cheap: it prints two blanks ('8-5=___', '8-3=___') and verify.json declares TWO eval entries under id 6, one per blank. The generator already knows how to cover several slots under one id; it simply did not apply that to the cross-out selections in problems 3 and 4.

The study guide's watch-out box states the one structural fact this whole topic turns on: 'Turning an adding fact around (5 + 4 instead of 4 + 5) makes a new fact, but turning a take-away fact around does not --- 10 - 3 and 10 - 7 are different facts, while writing 10 - 7 twice is the same fact twice.' That sentence is the diagnosis for every find-and-fix item on the sheet.

Every answer-key solution ends with a check that closes the bond ('check by adding the parts back together: 4 + 2 = 6'), so the key models the self-verification habit rather than only producing the number.

The two planted wrong results are declared traps with the misconception spelled out (12 = added instead of taking away; a repeated 9-7=2), and they print in the key's Common wrong answers block -- which is exactly what the prompt asked for.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md actively steers error-analysis items away from 'manual': 'error-analysis ("find and fix the mistake") via the ordinary types --- the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right. Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning.' A find-and-fix item has TWO halves: the correction (checkable) and the diagnosis (not). The instruction covers only the first half, so the generator types the whole problem as eval/solve and the honest manual flag is never raised.
evidence: worksheet problem 2: 'Tell a friend why 12 cannot be a part of 9. Then write the part that really goes in the circle.' -- verify.json id 2 is a lone eval (9-3 -> 6), no manual entry
final_response.md: 'Nothing is flagged manual --- every item on this sheet has a single checkable number.'
SKILL.md: 'error-analysis ("find and fix the mistake") via the ordinary types ... Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning'

root_causes.description: The coverage contract is stated per PROBLEM, not per printed RESPONSE SLOT. SKILL.md's JSON-format section says verification 'hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check', and verify.py enforces exactly that. One check therefore discharges a problem that prints two or three separate things for the student to write, and the gate chain reports the sheet as fully verified.
evidence: worksheet problem 3: 'Cross out the fact Ben wrote twice. Then write the take-away fact that is missing: 9 - 2 = ___' -- two responses, verify.json id 3 holds one eval entry (9-2 -> 7)
worksheet problem 4: 'Cross out the repeat, then write the missing take-away fact: 10 - 6 = ___' -- verify.json id 4 holds one eval entry (10-6 -> 4)
SKILL.md JSON-format section: 'verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check' -- one check per id is the whole contract
the same file already proves multi-entry ids work: id 6 carries two eval entries, one per printed blank

improvements.title: Explanations and drawn/marked work must be declared manual, not folded into a numeric check
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md so that a find-and-fix or error-analysis item is declared as TWO entries under one id: the ordinary typed check for the correction, plus a `manual` entry whose `desc` states the full-credit diagnosis. Extend the same rule to any stem containing 'explain', 'tell what ... did wrong', 'draw', 'cross out', 'circle', 'show your work' or 'write the equation'. Back it with a lint in tests/check_layout.py that scans problem prose for those verbs and fails when the matching id carries no `manual` entry. For this case the fix is two entries under id 2: the existing eval for the corrected part (6) plus {"type": "manual", "desc": "Child must say a part can never be larger than its whole, so 12 cannot sit under a 9."}.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a worksheet whose problem 2 reads 'Explain what she did wrong, then write the correct answer' with a verify JSON holding only an eval entry for id 2. Assert the build exits non-zero (or exit 2 with problem 2 listed as manual). Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text claims '0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the false '0 manual' claim on every misconception-analysis sheet. In this shard the same defect drives the REJECT on curr-019, curr-025, curr-026, curr-038 and curr-044 -- five of ten cases.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over prose will produce false positives (a stem that says 'draw' inside a worked hint). Ship it as exit-2 manual visibility rather than exit-1, which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

improvements.title: Every printed response slot needs its own verification entry, not one per problem
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule from 'one check per problem id' to 'one check per printed response slot'. Concretely: (a) rewrite the SKILL.md JSON-format sentence to require an entry for every blank, box or \ansblank the item prints, using a `manual` entry when a slot is a mark or a sentence; (b) have tests/check_layout.py count the response macros inside each \problem segment and fail when that count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying that id. The schema already supports several entries per id -- id 6 of this very file already carries two eval entries, one per printed blank, so the change is a rule change plus a checker, not a schema change.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints two \ansblank slots with a verify JSON carrying a single entry for id 1, and assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming problem 1. It passes (exit 0) today, which is the defect.
improvements.expected_impact: Problems 3 and 4 gain an entry (or a manual entry) for the cross-out selection, so the key can state which of Ben's four facts is the duplicate instead of leaving the grader to infer it.
improvements.risk: Medium. Counting response macros will initially fire on sheets that print a decorative underline, and on the 'Answer:' line that some templates emit in addition to an inline blank. Land the checker in warn-only mode for one run, tune against the existing eval corpus, then make it a hard gate.

case_summary: The number-bond mathematics, the answer key and the study guide are all correct and genuinely well pitched: a warm-up, three find-and-fix items whose planted errors are distinct (a part larger than the whole, a duplicated take-away fact, an adding fact standing where a take-away fact belongs), a fill-the-blank, and a challenge that needs both missing facts. Every printed value recomputes. The rejection is entirely about the verification trust boundary: problem 2's 'tell a friend why' explanation and the required cross-out selections in problems 3 and 4 are unverified and undeclared, while the delivery text states that nothing on the sheet is manual. Both defects trace to SKILL.md rather than to this case -- the per-problem coverage rule and the instruction to route error-analysis through the ordinary types.
